title: parseSortParam: unrecognized sort names must pass through, empty ones must be dropped
answers: What happens if a search sort field name isn't recognized?
Can I add validation/error on unknown sort values in dashboard search?
Why does an empty or '-' sort param get skipped instead of sent to the backend?
body:
In pkg/registry/apis/dashboard/search.go, `parseSortParam` must return the field unchanged (not empty, not an error) when it doesn't match `uiSortAliases` or `searchsort.ParseSortName` — this lets the backend's `search_enforce_sort_capability` check report a genuine capability violation for misspelled/unsupported fields instead of the client swallowing the mistake.
Separately, when `parseSortParam` returns an empty field (raw sort was `""` or just `"-"`), the caller in `convertHttpSearchRequestToResourceSearchRequest` must `continue` and skip appending to `SortBy` rather than sending an empty-field sort entry to the backend.
If either behavior is removed: unknown fields would either error incorrectly (blocking legit-but-unmapped sorts) or be silently accepted (hiding the field-name bug), and empty sorts would send a malformed sort entry to resource search.
